generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The local field in `MergeResult` is still named `trackArraySource` (the LHS of every assignment in this diff), while the rest of the codebase has been renamed to `storeArraySource`. This is a naming inconsistency that will confuse readers — the field should be renamed to `storeArraySource` to match the new convention. As written, a developer reading this block sees `trackArraySource = mergeWithObject.storeArraySource` which reads as if two different concepts are being conflated.

The array-filtering logic builds a `Set<String> arrays` from `NameValue::name` and checks `arrays.contains(field.fieldName())`. However, the `NameValue.name` is set to a **full path** (e.g., `"path.to"`) for non-root cases (see `#9H8GF`: `context.parent().name() + "." + arrayFieldName`), while `field.fieldName()` likely returns the **simple** field name (e.g., `"to"`). If that's the case, the `contains` check will never match, the field will be written both as a regular field *and* as part of the ignored value, producing duplicate data in the synthetic source.
Please verify that `field.fieldName()` returns the same fully-qualified name that is stored in `NameValue.name`. If it returns only the simple name, the comparison should use `ignored.getFieldName()` (the simple name) instead of `ignored.name`.

review_comment: This is a new usage of the switchParser() method. However it is currently deprecated. I think if we like to use then we should un-deprecate this method. I think this new usage is a valid use case. cc: @javanna

Looking at the concerns we had with switchParser, i think your assessment is right. Also, its javadocs says

>  we are actively deprecating and removing the ability to pass complex objects to multifields, so try and avoid using this method

Given that this was committed 4 years ago, the "actively" part no longer holds true. I reviewed the current usages of switchParser and they seem ok to me. I have a slight concern that we are now using the method in a general utility method, that may spread its usage instead of limiting it to the only places where it's strictly needed. I am not sure what to do about that though, and I am ok with the current plan. Thanks for raising this.
